newsitem.title: UK: British treasure raises $2.5 million at auction.
newsitem.headline: British treasure raises $2.5 million at auction.

text.p: A hoard of gold coins and other treasures salvaged from the wreck of British steamer The Douro raised 1.5 million pounds ($2.5 million) in a two-day auction which ended on Thursday.
"Bidding was constant throughout the two days," said auctioneers Spink and Son in a statement.
"The magic of a deep sea wreck caught the imagination of coin collectors and souvenir hunters worldwide."
The amount raised was in line with the auctioneer's estimate and included the buyers' 10 percent premium.

The Douro sank with the loss of 17 lives in 1882 after colliding with the Spanish steamer Yrurac Bat. Salvage experts found its remains after a remote-controlled undersea camera revealed one the ship's crested porcelain dinner plates embedded in the sand.
The ship had been bringing wealthy passengers back from a voyage to South America and had 28,000 gold sovereigns dating from the reign of Britain's Queen Victoria in its safe.
The haul also included a small number of Brazilian coins.
